subject: Geography
unit: Spring 2: Weather, climate and climate change
source: Written for geography/y8 lesson 11 (Climate graphs sheet with data (portal printable; data from published climate averages))
intro: Lesson 11: Tropical cyclones and climates around the world. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Tropical cyclones
points: Hurricane, typhoon or cyclone by ocean
Form over seas of about 27 degrees C or more
Between about 5 and 30 degrees from the equator

panels.title: Climate factors
points: Distance from the sea, winds, currents

model.title: Describe the climate of a Mediterranean city from its graph

parts.text: Pattern: hot dry summers, mild wet winters

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Use data: 'the hottest month is July at about 27 degrees C'

keywords.def: a huge, powerful low-pressure storm that forms over warm seas
how far a place is from the sea
a chart showing average temperature and rainfall for each month

questions.q: Explain why tropical cyclones lose strength over land. (2 marks)
questions.a: They are cut off from warm, moist sea air (1), which is their energy source (1)

questions.q: Core: Annotate a tropical cyclone formation diagram, then describe two climate graphs (a tropical and a polar place) using data.
Extend: Explain how altitude affects climate using an example.
questions.a: Temperature falls with height, so mountains like the Andes are cooler than lowlands at the same latitude

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why the UK has a mild maritime climate.
questions.a: Latitude, sea all around, North Atlantic Drift and westerly winds

questions.q: Tropical cyclones need sea temperatures of at least about:
questions.a: B) 27 degrees C. Warm water provides the heat and moisture that power the storm.

questions.q: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone in the:
Big question: why do hurricanes never form over the UK?
questions.a: UK seas are too cool (well below about 27 degrees C) and we are too far from the tropics
